title: Design System: A History of Tufted Rugs

shade-teal.note: Per-page token --shade; shade ink = color-mix(in oklab, var(--shade), #000 22%) in light, #fff 18% in dark.

display.purpose: Cover title only; Archivo at 82% width.

headline.purpose: Chapter and page titles; chapter titles max 18ch.

shade-number.purpose: 'Shade N' beside the wound band (1.5rem) and in contents rows (0.9375rem).

body.purpose: Chapter prose in Literata at a 37rem measure.

dek.purpose: Chapter dek under the title, roman not italic, ink-2.

pull.purpose: Pull quotes at 32ch under a shade thread.

frame.purpose: Default page text outside the reading column; panels, end matter.

label.purpose: Navigation, buttons, chips, byline; sentence case, no tracking.

extensions.elevation: Flat. Tonal layers board / ground / sheet plus 1px hairlines and 2px ink or shade rules; no box-shadow.

derived.name: shade-ink
derived.purpose: Note numbers, Source links, ready-chapter status, focus ring.

derived.name: note-target
derived.purpose: Highlight of the targeted note in the end matter.

motion.name: scroll-progress

motion.purpose: 2px shade thread under the masthead on chapter pages, where scroll timelines are supported.

breakpoints.name: margin-fold
breakpoints.note: Margin notes fold into tap-to-open panels; margin figures enter the flow.

breakpoints.name: dates-list
breakpoints.note: Key-dates thread becomes a vertical list.

breakpoints.name: single-column
breakpoints.note: End matter and record pages go single column.

breakpoints.name: timeline-compact

breakpoints.name: mobile
breakpoints.note: Contents rows stack; reference links single column; smaller chapter band.

narrative.overview:
The history is laid out like a dye house's yarn shade card: a cool, card-stock grey sheet with one band of wound yarn per chapter, each with its shade number. The cover is the card itself, thirteen shades in a single bordered sheet; a chapter is one shade picked off that card and read. A charcoal bookcloth board closes the page top and bottom, the way a sample book's covers hold its cards. The world owns the frame (masthead, bands, shade numbers, headings, rules); the reading column stays calm.

Density is that of a close-reading book page: a single text measure with a margin column beside it where every note sits next to the sentence it supports and links to its record in one step. The world is flat and matter-of-fact, made of tonal sheets, hairline rules and condensed type rather than shadows or ornament. Its honesty is visible design, not small print: the prototype notice under the masthead, "Permission pending" on uncleared pictures, the count of sources "checked at the archive", and the "Still to find" panel are part of the system.

The world refuses the cream-paper editorial long-read: serif display headings on off-white, italic deks, small tracked labels above headings.
keyCharacteristics: Cool grey card-stock ground, never cream; charcoal board for masthead and foot only.
One chapter shade per page, drawn as a wound-yarn band and reused as the page's only accent.
Condensed Archivo for the frame and headings, Literata for reading, tabular numerals for dates and shade numbers.
A text column with a margin-note column; every note, picture and date opens its record.
Flat surfaces separated by tone and 1-2px rules; no shadows.
Status (prototype, permission, verification, gaps) shown in plain words.

rules.name: The Card-Stock Rule
rules.body: The ground is cool grey card (#e6e9e4), never cream, ivory or warm paper.

rules.name: The One Shade Rule
rules.body: A page carries one chapter shade and every accent on it derives from that shade; no second accent colour is introduced. Other cloths appear only as a chapter's own band or swatch.

rules.name: The Board Rule
rules.body: The charcoal board is the binding: masthead and foot, nothing else. Content never sits on a dark panel.

rules.name: The Frame and Read Rule
rules.body: Archivo for the frame: headings, navigation, captions, notes, labels, data. Literata for reading: prose, deks, the scope line, pull quotes, citations, timeline event titles, bibliography entries.

rules.name: The Condensed Heading Rule
rules.body: Headings are Archivo at 82-90% width, weight 650-700, with slight negative tracking. A serif display heading breaks the world.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Years, shade numbers, note numbers and counts set in tabular lining numerals.

rules.name: The Margin Column Rule
rules.body: Sources sit beside the sentence, not at the bottom of the screen: 37rem text plus a 14rem note column on wide screens; on narrow screens a tap opens the note in place rather than jumping to the end.

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Surfaces sit flat at rest and in every state; hover changes a border, underline or text colour, never adds lift.

rules.name: The One-Step Rule
rules.body: Every note, figure, key date and timeline event links straight to its record page; the record links on to the holding institution.

rules.name: The Visible Status Rule
rules.body: Prototype, "Permission pending", "checked at the archive" counts, "not yet checked at the source" and "Still to find" are shown in plain words at full legibility, never hidden, greyed out of reach or styled away.

dos: **Do** set the page ground to Card-Stock Grey (#e6e9e4) and keep the charcoal board (#1e2421) for masthead and foot.
**Do** set `--shade` once per page from the chapter's cloth and take every accent (band, threads, note numbers, Source links, focus ring) from it.
**Do** show a chapter's shade as a wound band with its shade number and cloth name ("Shade 6, Teal"), never as a bare colour.
**Do** set headings in Archivo at 82-90% width, weight 650-700, and reading text in Literata at a 37rem measure.
**Do** put sources in the 14rem margin beside the text and link each to its record in one step.
**Do** use tabular numerals for years, shade numbers and counts.
**Do** show permission and verification status in words wherever the image or claim appears.
donts: **Don't** use cream, ivory or warm off-white grounds.
**Don't** set headings in a serif display face, put deks in italic, or place small tracked uppercase labels above headings.
**Don't** introduce a second accent colour on a chapter page, or use another chapter's cloth outside its own band or swatch.
**Don't** add box-shadows, lift on hover, or rounded corners beyond 3px.
**Don't** draw the band as a flat swatch, gradient or random noise; it is exact parallel strands, the same every render.
**Don't** put content on the dark board or hide status marks to tidy a page.
